correctness.rationale: The positive Clebsch–Gordan coefficients and Haar orthonormality give a coefficientwise triangle-inequality reduction; the moduli of every complex optimizer therefore solve the nonnegative problem. Counting the overlaps of the three product intervals for χ_n², χ_nχ_{2n}, and χ_{2n}² recovers the stated parity polynomial. Write H_n(v)=nf(v)+g(v) for the normalized two-mode profile at angle v. At a fixed angle the cost of reallocating squared coefficient mass a² to χ_0 is (2a²−a⁴)H_n, while the linear benefit is 4aR(v). Since f≥1, comparison with a=0 at that angle forces every maximizing a to be O(1/n), uniformly. The a-stationarity equation near the leading angular maximum then gives a=R(v)/(nf(v))+O(n^-2), and profiling adds 2R(v)²/(nf(v))+O(n^-2). Uniqueness, interiority and nondegeneracy of the leading maxima give O(1/n) angular displacement in both optimizations, so evaluating the profiled addition at their respective angles sandwiches the optimal gain with the claimed remainder. For odd n, maximizing 2+2x²−3x⁴ gives x²=1/3 and f*=7/3; for even n the angular ratio x/y=√3−1 follows from the derivative's only positive zero, with f*=2(x+y)². Substitution verifies both stated gain coefficients, both trivial-mode scales, and both higher-mode limits. At every finite n an interior two-mode maximizer is available: the odd quadratic vertex is interior, and the even equal-weight trial beats both pure modes. Its right derivative in the anchor direction is positive. Thus strict gain is not inferred merely from an asymptotic or a numerical check.
residual_risks: No complete finite-n classification of optimizer phases is claimed. The recorded numerical stress cases and Haar quadratures were not rerun and are not needed by the proof.

originality.rationale: The same-day indexed two-character theorem exactly covers B_n by specialization and receives full credit for that baseline, without inferring a priority ordering from the date. It does not cover the third-mode perturbation. The earlier fixed-offset theorem does not apply to these widening gaps and would not resolve an O(1/n) difference with an O(1) error. The distinct supported contribution is the strict gain, explicit parity-specific first-order difference and optimizer scale for the anchored packet.

value.rationale: The addition of the identity representation is a canonical augmentation of the sparse high-mode packet. Resolving the first nonzero gain, although much smaller than either norm's leading order, quantifies the tradeoff between high-mode norm loss and new low-mode interference, and locates the optimal amount of coefficient mass in the new degree of freedom for every optimizer. The different constants arise from an exact parity effect in fusion, not unrelated finite samples.
residual_risks: The claimed value is the anchored sensitivity and its optimizer scaling, not a general compact-group inequality or a new two-character formula.
